purpose: Push the exact linear-hash barrier from one to two syndrome coordinates. First classify when a rank-two GF(3) matrix A can have 0 absent from A{+/-1}^m using the four projective directions of PG(1,3). Then use cycle-space support constraints to show that neither zero-free projective pattern can occur when A is a rank-two projection of the cycle matrix of a simple graph. Thus every rank-two syndrome zero-test also has a zero witness, even on an uncolourable simple graph.

rank2_projective_setup.matrix: A is a rank-two matrix over GF(3), with arbitrary zero columns allowed.
rank2_projective_setup.sign_image: T(A)={A s : s in {+1,-1}^m} subset GF(3)^2.
rank2_projective_setup.directions: Every nonzero column belongs to one of exactly four projective lines of PG(1,3). Let n_L be the multiplicity of direction L among nonzero columns.
one_direction_contribution: If n_L=0 the contribution set is {0}.
If n_L=1 the contribution set is L minus {0}: the two nonzero scalar multiples of one representative.
If n_L>=2 the contribution set is the whole line L, because two independently signed nonzero collinear columns already realize scalar sums 0,+1,-1 and further columns only add translations inside L.

classification_theorem.name: RANK2_SIGN_IMAGE_ZERO_FREE_PROJECTIVE_PATTERNS
classification_theorem.statement: For rank(A)=2, 0 is absent from T(A) iff either (I) exactly two projective directions are occupied and at least one of the two has multiplicity one, or (II) all four projective directions are occupied and every multiplicity equals one.
proof: Exactly two occupied directions: if both multiplicities are at least two, both line-contribution sets contain zero, so zero is attainable. If one direction occurs once, its contribution is always one nonzero vector on that line; the sum cannot be cancelled by any vector from a distinct line. Thus zero is absent iff at least one multiplicity is one.

Exactly three occupied directions: if all are singletons, the three representatives in a 2D space have a unique linear dependence and, because no two are parallel, every dependence coefficient is nonzero; over GF(3) the coefficients are +/-1, giving a signed zero sum. If one direction is repeated, quotient by that line. The other two nonzero projective directions both map to nonzero elements of the one-dimensional quotient, and their signs can be chosen to cancel; the repeated line then cancels the residual exactly. Hence zero is always attainable.

All four directions occupied: if some direction is repeated, quotient by it. The other three directions contribute three independently sign-flippable nonzero elements of GF(3); choose their projected signs all equal, whose sum is 3=0, and cancel the remaining residual in the repeated line. If all four are singletons, after a GL(2,3) change of basis the directions are e1,e2,e1+e2,e1-e2. Solving +/-e1 +/-e2 +/- (e1+e2) +/- (e1-e2)=0 forces one coordinate sign to be zero, impossible. Therefore this unique four-singleton pattern is zero-free.
Rank two excludes the one-direction case. These exhaust PG(1,3).

graphic_corollary.setup: Let G be a simple graph, Q a full-row-rank GF(3) cycle matrix, and H a rank-two linear map on syndrome space. Put A=H Q. Because Q has a right inverse on its row space, rank(A)=rank(H)=2, and both rows of A lie in the cycle/flow space of G.
case_I_impossible: Suppose exactly two projective column directions occur and one direction L_s occurs on exactly one edge e.
Choose a nonzero linear functional phi on GF(3)^2 that vanishes on the other projective line L_o but not on L_s.
Then phi A is a nonzero cycle-space vector supported only on e; zero columns and all L_o columns vanish, while the unique L_s column survives.
A loopless graph has no nonzero one-edge flow, contradicting incidence conservation. Thus case I cannot occur even for loopless multigraphs.
case_II_impossible: If all four projective directions occur exactly once, the union of supports of the two independent cycle-space rows of A has exactly four edges.
Therefore the 2D row space of A is contained in the cycle space of the simple four-edge subgraph induced by those support edges.

Every simple graph with at most four edges has cycle rank at most one: two independent cycles require at least five edges in one component (or at least six edges if cycle rank is split across components).
Hence a four-edge simple subgraph cannot contain a 2D cycle space, contradiction.
graphic_corollary.theorem: For every simple graph and every rank-two syndrome projection H, 0 belongs to {H Qs : s in {+1,-1}^E}.
graphic_corollary.uncolourable_false_positive: If the simple graph is not 3-colourable then no full syndrome Qs is zero, but every rank-two projected zero-test still has at least one sign vector with H Qs=0. Thus rank-two linear compression cannot be zero-reflecting on any uncolourable simple source graph.

positive: The complete rank-two image question reduces to four projective multiplicities; no sign-cube enumeration is needed.
Graphic cycle-space constraints eliminate both abstract zero-free rank-two patterns for simple graphs.
killed: Compress the cycle syndrome to any two GF(3) linear checks and decide non-colourability from absence/presence of projected zero.
Search over polynomially many rank-two hashes hoping one becomes zero-reflecting on a simple Hamiltonian hard instance; none can.
Use a pair of checksum/cycle characters as a complete substitute for the linear-size mixed-cycle syndrome.
not_killed: Nonlinear compression or an interlacement contraction not expressible as a fixed low-rank linear projection.
Formula-dependent iterative contractions that prove safety at each step by stronger graphic structure.

next_target.name: E8_GRAPHIC_RANK3_PROJECTIVE_SYNDROME_CLASSIFICATION_V5_9
next_target.directive: Move to rank three only after exploiting PG(2,3) geometry. Classify small-support/projective configurations of columns of A=H Q that can avoid signed zero, then intersect those configurations with simple-graphic cycle-space restrictions. Do not enumerate 3^beta syndromes or 2^E sign vectors. A useful outcome is either a rank-three universal false-positive theorem or a sharply characterized exceptional configuration that can serve as a source-certified contraction target.
